observations: Footman and Knight give the clearest plate-armour comparison. Footman separates a large white-rimmed shield, red team-colour shoulder caps and a pale helmet face from a darker torso. Knight repeats bright edged armour and gold decoration across both rider and horse. The Knight's 45-triangle horse covering carries painted medallions, and its five-triangle straps carry painted studs. A rich mounted silhouette therefore does not imply a separate mesh for every gold detail.

Footman's nine-triangle shield front includes the white rim as paint; its eight-triangle central boss supplies actual relief. The helmet shell/visor costs 47 triangles and the face/moustache another 44. Two nine-triangle shoulder caps obtain their rounded reading partly from curved painted highlights. Those particular counts explain how Footman spends more on recognition around the head than on a rim around the shield; they are not universal armour budgets.

Mountain King and Rifleman make dwarf identity differently from Footman's enclosed head. Mountain King's 123-triangle helmet/face/beard assembly is supplemented by a twenty-triangle moustache and separate four-triangle eyebrows; Rifleman's face/beard costs 94 with a separate 23-triangle moustache. Their large facial silhouettes remain distinct from the surrounding armour or hood. Mountain King's twelve-triangle box hammer has painted inner bevels, whereas Rifleman's weapon begins with a 32-triangle stock/barrel body plus separate fittings and alpha cards.

TownHall, HumanBarracks and Farm keep building materials in broad readable zones: pale masonry, wood framing/doors and a large roof. TownHall and HumanBarracks use red team-colour roof fields in these captures; Farm uses fixed yellow thatch and a red door. HumanBarracks can carry a large roof panel in four triangles and a tower roof cap in four, while Farm's chimney pots use thirteen triangles including a five-sided opening. Painted brick joints and thatch strands supply detail without corresponding masonry blocks or individual straws.

This reviewed human set is not one body proportion: Rifleman is dominated by hood, beard and a long gun; Mountain King by beard and paired blunt weapons; Knight by the combined horse/rider. Their common bright metal and bordered colour fields are visible in the named sheets below, but those material choices do not erase the different silhouettes. The High Elf/Blood Elf sources are compared separately because they share a gameplay roster without sharing the dwarf head proportions.

observations: Grunt and HeroBladeMaster both expose large green shoulder/arm masses, but the weapon and back silhouette distinguish them. Grunt pairs a compact heavy axe with blocky boots and a low head. HeroBladeMaster adds a long narrow blade, a tall bent banner pole and a broad emblem field. The banner costs twelve triangles; its gold emblem is paint. The 14-triangle pole provides its bend geometrically, so the outline survives even when the emblem is too small to read.

Grunt's connected head/jaw/tusk assembly is 130 triangles, with separate five-triangle ears and a two-triangle long facial tusk elsewhere. Its axe blade and haft are eight triangles each; the haft has three sides at the measured sections. Each eight-triangle shoulder plate carries the irregular pale fur border on the same painted surface. This is a concrete instance where facial mass and silhouette receive geometry while a furry edge on armour remains paint.

Tauren, Headhunter and WitchDoctor prevent an orc profile from collapsing into green skin. Tauren's bull head, torso and arms form a 234-triangle assembly; the fourteen-triangle totem carries painted end grain, wraps and large glyphs. Headhunter and WitchDoctor use blue skin, long tusks and pointed ears in the reviewed captures. Headhunter's head is 113 triangles and its tusks fifteen each; WitchDoctor's head is eighty and tusks nine each. Their shared motif is elongated facial anatomy, but the measured parts differ substantially.

Shaman's pale animal pelt produces another distinct outer contour. The body/pelt assembly has 262 triangles, with nine-triangle claw ornaments and four-triangle collar strips carrying painted chain links. GreatHall and WatchTower repeat large timber forms at architectural scale: GreatHall's radial roof planes and pale ribs surround a central peak; WatchTower exposes a tall braced timber support under a six-triangle, seven-position roof. The tower's roof is a geometric six-sided pyramid, while wood grain and binding marks are painted.

HeroBladeMaster's two-triangle hoop earring, Tauren's two-triangle nose-ring card and Shaman's painted chain strips show three ways to suggest small curved metal forms without fully round geometry. The chain, ring and banner observations belong to these specific sources. LowPolyWorks' Aspiring Champion uses the same broader idea of selective detail but spends 36 triangles on individual raised studs; that owner example should not be substituted for the native orc counts.

observations: Skeleton, HeroLich and HeroDeathKnight all place pale bone-like marks against darker fields, but their construction is not interchangeable. Skeleton's skull including jaw is a 126-triangle connected mesh. HeroDeathKnight's five-triangle skull-faced armour plate and seven-triangle hanging plates carry the eye sockets as paint. A small skull emblem can therefore be a shaped plate, whereas the head that defines Skeleton's identity is a much fuller object.

Skeleton's 52-triangle ribcage/pelvis has internal rib divisions predominantly painted. HeroLich instead includes a thirty-triangle open chest frame and a separate twelve-triangle striped torso surface. HeroLich's 210-triangle head/crown/spiked collar is one combined rigid assembly, with a separate 32-triangle jaw. Calling that whole assembly a skull would inflate skull statistics and lose the crown and shoulders that make the silhouette wide.

HeroLich's floating ragged edge is assembled from eight five-triangle robe strips and three longer ten-triangle strips, with small dark lining strips behind some surfaces. Painted folds and borders strengthen the shape, but the separated strips create the real outer gaps. Necromancer has a different cloth construction: a 22-triangle main skirt and ten-triangle sleeves, topped by a 166-triangle horned animal skull headdress. Its horns and skull are one component; their growth bands and dark cavities are painted.

CryptFiend and Gargoyle supply non-humanoid signatures. CryptFiend combines a broad grey arched shell with a pale striped front, thin legs and detached small spikes; ten spikes cost three triangles each and four others five each. Gargoyle separates dark thin wing membranes from long angular red team-colour fingers in this preview. Four large membrane components are two triangles each, while six finger components cost five each. Its head/hair assembly costs 191 triangles compared with 163 for the headless body.

Necropolis links these contrasts to architecture through dark sloping walls, pale edge ribs, red banners and a skull at the entrance. Acolyte uses a deep dark hood with a small pale face and bright bordered trim. These sources make an undead palette more specific than 'black and green': pale faces/bone, dark grey or purple structural fields, selected saturated identity patches and sharp light borders. The precise native region and its source model remain necessary when reusing the paint; the whole sheet is not uniformly bone or cloth.

observations: Archer, EX_Dryad and Huntress share pale purple skin and sharply pointed ears in the reviewed captures, but differ in carrier anatomy. Archer stands on two legs with a broad team-colour cloak and long angular bow. EX_Dryad joins an elf upper body to a deer-like four-legged body. Huntress places the rider above a dark cat. This variety means an elf profile must retain what the body sits on; the overall unit height alone cannot describe the proportions.

Archer's body/head/arms/armour form one 307-triangle component, with a 24-triangle recurved bow, twelve-triangle quiver and 33-triangle cloak. EX_Dryad's head is 114 triangles and its animal body 148; ears cost six each and hooves nine each. Its spear's leaf-shaped end uses two perpendicular four-triangle cards. Leaf imagery is therefore sometimes painted cutout geometry, rather than a thin solid leaf or a fully rounded spearhead.

Huntress's reviewed rider body is 232 triangles and the mount body 221. Four two-triangle alpha cards carry the cat's claws, and an inspected fang has two oppositely wound faces sharing three positions. These details make the mount's face and feet readable without small closed solids everywhere. Huntress's dark cat, silver rimmed glaive and purple rider also differ strongly from EX_Dryad's warm brown animal body and green leaf details.

DruidoftheClaw uses a 112-triangle hood with a visible bear mouth around the head, while the alternative full bear body is a separate 366-triangle component hidden in the sampled caster pose. HeroDemonHunter's head/hair is 141 triangles plus a 27-triangle topknot; its body is 119. Long ears, long hair and curved paired weapons create its elf silhouette without requiring foliage on the body.

TreeofLife and AncientofWar carry faces, bark masses, root-like limbs, green canopy patches and heavy stone-like plates. Their 698 and 736 sampled body triangles belong to articulated living architecture, rather than a small hut with tree paint. The reviewed Night Elf set thus uses at least four distinct material arrangements: Archer's cloak/skin/metal, EX_Dryad's skin/fur/leaves, DruidoftheClaw's animal pelt and the Ancients' bark/foliage/stone. The sheets and mapped regions in the table preserve those differences.

observations: NagaMyrmidon and NagaRoyalGuard show a broad finned head/shoulder mass over a coiled tail, with blue-green skin and a large bright gold weapon. Their sampled bodies are 563 and 581 triangles, each using one visible diffuse sheet. NagaSiren narrows the upper body and carries a long tail with an extended fin edge; HeroNagaSeawitch adds a larger ornamented head/shoulder arrangement and a bow. The latter two are 604 and 822 triangles. These are whole-body observations; they do not establish an isolated fin or tail budget.

The reviewed NagaMyrmidon, NagaRoyalGuard and NagaSiren captures place cyan/green painted skin next to warm yellow-gold edges. Sharp head fins, weapon points and tail fins project beyond the main torso. HeroNagaSeawitch preserves the long tail carrier while adding broad dark-gold ornament and a more prominent ranged weapon. Red identity areas in this red-player preview must be distinguished from the underlying fixed blue-green skin.

SnapDragon belongs to the official naga roster but has a low four-legged, long-bodied profile instead of a humanoid torso and tail. Its blue body has a pronounced dark dorsal fin line and long pointed snout. TempleofTides uses an upright serpentine form within a stone platform, CoralBed combines a pillar and branching coral colours around a low base, and TidalGuardian places a turquoise creature in a raised basin with tall curved corner forms. Those named examples connect marine motifs across creatures and buildings without assuming every naga object is a snake-bodied person.

The reviewed units each use one visible diffuse path, while TempleofTides uses three and CoralBed and TidalGuardian two. The building and unit counts include their sampled visible geometry only, excluding hidden construction/death alternatives. Detailed fin cross-sections and painted-versus-solid ornament boundaries were not manually traced for this Naga sample; the profile records visible silhouettes, actual sheet assignments and numeric model evidence, leaving those narrower component claims unresolved.

observations: Gnoll, Kobold, Ogre and Murloc do not form one silhouette family even though the installed object rows group them as creeps. Gnoll has a long muzzle and hunched furred upper body; Kobold is compact under oversized ear/head shapes and equipment; the reviewed two-headed Ogre has a broad bare torso and blunt club; Murloc places a very large round-eyed head over a small narrow body and legs. Their sampled bodies are 378, 266, 494 and 358 triangles. A single creep median would conceal precisely the head and body choices that identify these creatures.

ForestTroll, IceTroll and DarkTroll each have 421 sampled body triangles and one visible diffuse sheet. In the reviewed captures their posture and extended arm/ear shapes correspond closely, while skin changes from green through pale cyan to purple. Equal counts alone do not prove identical vertex positions, UVs or rigging; this profile records a visually corresponding family and exact counts, not an unmeasured clone claim. The sheet paths retain the three painted variants rather than collapsing them into a generic troll skin.

Ogre and OgreMagi both have 494 sampled body triangles. OgreMagi's blue skin and strong dark body markings contrast with Ogre's tan skin while preserving the visible two-head, broad torso and club arrangement. Furbolg instead reads through a large brown furry body, broad paws and coloured projecting ornaments, at 288 sampled triangles. Satyr uses a narrower horned humanoid profile with cloven-looking lower limbs and long pointed head extensions, at 404. Those fur, skin and ornament regions cannot be inferred safely from the common category label.

Tuskar uses a compact brown-and-pale body, prominent tusks and a pale blue weapon, at 534 sampled triangles. Magnataur spreads a furred mammoth-like carrier across four feet with a large upper body and long tusks, at 851. In the directly inspected Magnataur parts, the head/body/limbs form a 542-triangle connected assembly, four fur-covered feet cost fifteen each, and fur-fringe strips range from two to six triangles. Its polearm comprises a twenty-triangle blade, 27-triangle haft and four six-triangle head spikes. These are measured component boundaries, rather than estimates from the unit's bone names.

The Magnataur sheet is also an owner texture source: the reviewed Strigoi Vampire reuses it for skirt and waist pieces. That reuse selects pale/brown painted structure for a new humanoid garment rather than importing Magnataur's original mammoth anatomy. The original and reused component evidence is linked in the vampire study, demonstrating why the visual material library must allow a creature sheet to supply cloth-like or trim-like areas.

Harpy's long feathered wings, pale body and small feet create a different flying silhouette from the dragons' dark membranes and projecting fingers. Its sampled body is 349 triangles. Centaur's 294-triangle body joins a humanoid tool-user to a four-legged carrier, while Hydra's 470-triangle body distributes recognition across multiple heads and a low long body. Nerubian's 368 triangles instead build a compact armoured upper mass over several narrow articulated legs. These specific carrier arrangements are more informative than treating all three as large monsters.

FacelessOne's purple flesh, prominent head appendages, silver bands and massive weapon contrast with Revenant's dark red-black armour and long upright weapon. FacelessOne is 440 sampled triangles and Revenant 364. Their sheets can offer material regions unrelated to the creature as a whole: the owner's reviewed Necrarch book ornament uses FacelessOne paint, while its book frame uses UndeadAirBarge. This transfer is supported by part-level UV records in the owner study, not by a guess from the source filename.

RockGolem has a blocky broken-rock outline and dense crack painting; ThunderLizard has a broad low green body, pale scale markings and a line of projecting dorsal plates. Their sampled bodies are 422 and 533 triangles. SludgeMonster uses a dark blue-purple mass and long pointed extensions at 267 triangles. These three demonstrate different ways to carry texture detail on large forms, but this profile does not claim that every visible crack, scale or tendril was separately traced. Exact painted-versus-modelled boundaries require the component/UV evidence for that part.

The selected creature creeps use one visible diffuse sheet each except RockGolem, which uses two, and Revenant, which uses three in this sample. Revenant combines its armour sheet with BlueWaves and Blue_Glow2 effect surfaces. The body counts exclude hidden alternatives and hero glow. These observations are useful reference families, not a universal quota for wings, scales, rock pieces or creature limbs.

Demoness uses a smaller horned humanoid silhouette with dark wings and warm red-orange skin; Felgaurd is a broad armoured humanoid with a large patterned blade; EredarWarlock places red skin and gold-black ornaments around an upright caster body. A generic 'red humanoid with horns' profile would omit the low quadruped, rock-bodied and massive multi-limbed examples in this same sample.

ChaosGrunt and ordinary Grunt each measure 421 sampled body triangles. The reviewed ChaosGrunt retains the recognisable axe, shoulder mass and low tusked head arrangement while changing exposed skin to red-orange and shifting surrounding paint. This is a visual/count comparison only, without claiming an exact geometry clone. Warcraft's ChaosGrunt is also a distinct source from LowPolyWorks' Warhammer Chaos armies: their names do not justify treating the materials, symbols or construction as identical.

observations: Sheep, Pig and Seal are the sparse end of this reviewed sample at 69, 70 and 52 sampled triangles. Sheep reads through a pale wool mass with dark face/feet; Pig through a warm mottled body and projecting snout; Seal through an elongated pale spotted body with flattened flippers. Their one-sheet designs concentrate recognition on broad body proportions and a small number of appendages, rather than on equipment.

BrownWolf and BlackStagMale rise to 168 and 212 sampled triangles. BrownWolf has a long narrow muzzle, pointed ears and a raised tail; BlackStagMale adds slender legs and antler branches around a leaner four-legged carrier. In the reviewed captures their fur markings vary substantially, even though both are small background animals. The independently fitted pictures do not prove the two animals have similar in-game heights.

Albatross and Penguin use very different bird outlines at 123 and 164 triangles. Albatross has outstretched wings with painted dark feather edges and a small central body; Penguin has an upright oval body with pale belly, dark flanks and projecting yellow head feathers. HermitCrab is the expensive outlier here at 398 triangles, distributing geometry over claws, legs and a large pale shell. This reviewed critter set therefore cannot support a rule that all ambient animals should be under one hundred triangles.

Each of the eight named critters uses one sampled visible diffuse path. Their texture names and UV captures provide material sources for wool, fur, feather and shell appearances even when a later kitbash has no relation to the source animal. This profile records appearance and whole-model measurements; it does not claim a complete individually labelled anatomical decomposition of these eight models.

profiles.title: High Elves, Blood Elves and civilian faces
profiles.scope: Classic SD art; MDX format version does not determine art tier
profiles.reviewMethod: Direct visual review of all selected full-model contact captures; component observations only where annotated evidence exists
observations: HighElfArcher, Priest, Sorceress, HeroBloodElf and BloodElfSpellThief share pale skin, pointed ears and strong bright metal or gold edging in the reviewed sample. HighElfArcher's light hair and pale face contrast with the purple skin and darker hair of the reviewed Night Elf Archer, while the cloak-and-bow arrangement remains visually comparable. Both sampled bodies have 417 triangles; this number alone is not proof of identical underlying geometry.

Priest uses pale robe surfaces with gold edging around a narrow upper body and long staff. Sorceress combines pale skin, flowing hair, team-colour cloth fields and bright shoulder/arm borders. HeroBloodElf broadens the silhouette with large gold-scrollwork shoulder shapes and a dark flared robe. BloodElfSpellThief combines a tall red-gold shield, long pale blade and a narrow armoured body. Their sampled body counts are 399, 427, 569 and 432, each with one visible diffuse path. The dark robe and ornate gold edges of HeroBloodElf are not the same material arrangement as Priest's broad white surfaces.

VillagerMan, VillagerWoman and VillagerKid show a separate civilian use of facial proportion and clothing. The adult man wears a pale broad-shouldered shirt over brown lower clothing; the woman has a pale blouse and a long brown skirt; the child has a disproportionately prominent pale head, short torso and simple brown clothing. Their sampled bodies are 311, 325 and 216 triangles. Those are observed meshes, not a proposed recipe for scaling an adult to make a child.

The official unit tables classify these civilian models as commoner while the elf models sit in the human gameplay roster. The visual comparison keeps both facts: roster membership provides searchable source context, while the particular skin, hair, cloth and silhouette in the named source models provides the art evidence. Detailed ear cross-sections and individual costume-region labels are available only where separately reviewed; this profile does not extrapolate them across every elf or civilian model.

limitations: Official race is an object gameplay field, not an exclusive visual style label. One native model can have several race assignments.
Profiles describe the selected explicitly named models, not unreviewed members of the entire roster.
Full-model appearance does not establish an isolated part topology; component claims require annotated component evidence.
Visible red is the research red-player sample and may be team colour; it is not automatically fixed pigment.
